body:
CLOSING A FINDING I LEFT OPEN, rather than leaving it as a "separate later candidate" nobody
revisits. THE SEMANTIC ABSTENTION FINDING IS ALREADY CLOSED, and it was closed by 0ca09c5 - the same
commit whose docstring I got wrong yesterday.

THE FINDING AS SCOUT AND I RECORDED IT: an abstaining provider and one measuring exactly 0.5 are
bit-identical in the published record, INCLUDING SUPPORT. That was the reason it was carved out as
later work.

VERIFIED ON CURRENT MAIN, cost.scala:

  :866  val semEstimate = semantic(unit, node)          the provider's own Estimate is kept
  :868  case Estimate.Missing(reason) => Map(CostTerm.Semantic -> reason)
  :955  val measured = terms.keySet -- semImputed.keySet
  :956  val support  = supportOf(measured, eligible, weights)

So the two cells differ in TWO published fields, not zero:

                        terms[Semantic]   imputedTerms        measured   support
  provider ABSTAINED    0.5 (substituted)  {Semantic -> why}   excludes   LOWER
  provider MEASURED 0.5 0.5 (real)         {}                  includes   HIGHER

The price is identical - missingSemantic is still substituted and the M0 decision stands - but the
RECORD is not. `imputedTerms` names the reason, and because `measured` subtracts the imputed keys,
the support weight is strictly lower for the abstention. The finding's own worst clause, "including
support", is the one most clearly false now.

WHY I AM POSTING RATHER THAN JUST DROPPING IT: this bead was carved out on the strength of a claim
that stopped being true, and carved-out work is exactly what nobody re-derives. I have now made the
same class of error twice in two days in the opposite direction - documenting a defect that was
already fixed in trace.scala, and here nearly leaving a fix uncredited because the carve-out was
written before it landed. A finding and its fix can pass each other in the dark.

NOTHING TO IMPLEMENT. No bead needs opening; if one exists for this residual it can close on this
evidence. Chief, this also removes one item from whatever sequencing you inherited on
bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9 - the successor work it was waiting for has already happened.

Unchanged: cand-62FAKD3SZ awaits collab review; cand-2QZH1W and cand-7KHF208 approved and blocked
solely on cand-1EE04B. All three refreshed within the last few minutes.
